cohort: The cohort consists of 250 married teenage girls aged 15-19 years who delivered in selected tertiary care centers in Jharkhand, India.
finding: Teenage pregnancies in Jharkhand are associated with high rates of maternal anemia, hypertensive disorders, and various neonatal complications, compounded by poor antenatal care and socio-demographic factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries were performed in 10.8% of cases, mainly due to fetal distress.
birth_weight: 15.2% of neonates had low birth weight, with most deliveries resulting in acceptable birth weights.
gest_age: 78.4% of deliveries were full-term, and 10.8% were preterm.
